subject: APAC-first pin vs global-fallback scenarios — next steps
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Liao <aisha.liao@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-05-29T14:02:00-07:00
Subject: APAC-first pin vs global-fallback scenarios — post-call recap

Thanks again for taking the time today, Aisha — appreciate the clear overview of Nimbus Health's constraints. Quick recap from our side and a couple of clarifying questions so we can size options and draft a concrete proposal.

High-level from the call:
- Priority: APAC-first processing and storage for patient-facing inference (PII).
- Secondary: Global fallback (US/EU) only in declared disaster scenarios with strict audit logging and SLA-triggered manual failover.
- Backups: You mentioned daily incremental and weekly full backups; need to confirm encryption and cross-region snapshot retention.
- Retention: Regulatory minimums vary by asset class — you flagged clinical notes (10 years) vs analytics logs (2 years).

Questions we need answered to finalize the scope (can reply inline):
1) Confirm which dataset buckets you consider PII (names, MRNs, full-text clinical notes) vs pseudonymized telemetry. We need an explicit list to map to residency controls.
2) For cross-region fallback: do you require automatic cold failover (automated DNS + restore) or manual activation by Nimbus ops? The difference changes RTO significantly.
3) For backups: do cross-region encrypted snapshots need to be retained outside APAC (e.g., for disaster recovery), or must backups also be APAC-only?
4) Logging/audit: What level of entry is required for each event (read, write, model-infer)? Example templates are helpful — your security team can share sample log schemas if available.

Attachments: initial-call-notes.pdf (high-level notes).

Next steps from Redwood: Monica will follow up with a short technical note describing region-pin behavior, expected RPO/RTO ranges for manual vs automatic failover, and options for encrypted snapshot flows. We'll also capture a simple heatmap that shows cost/latency tradeoffs by pinning strategy.

If we can get answers to the 4 bullets above by EOD Tuesday 5/31, we should be able to turn around an ops-level proposal and a prioritized runbook.

Best,
Sergio Alvarez
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0193

From: Aisha Liao <aisha.liao@nimbushealth.com>

Date: 2027-05-30T02:13:00+08:00
Subject: Re: APAC-first pin vs global-fallback scenarios — post-call recap

Sergio — thanks for the summary and clear next steps. Quick answers inline: 

> 1) Confirm which dataset buckets you consider PII
We consider the following PII: patient full name, MRN, DOB, full-text clinical notes, and any uploaded documents that include patient identifiers. Device telemetry and anonymized usage metrics are non-PII.

> 2) Automatic vs manual failover
We prefer manual activation for global fallback. Nimbus ops want to review and execute failover (we have a certified runbook). Automatic failover to non-APAC without our approval is a no-go.

> 3) Backups — cross-region retention
Cross-region snapshots are allowed for disaster recovery but must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK). Prefer retention in a secondary APAC region where possible; only if required for legal reasons should we replicate to US/EU.

> 4) Logging/audit
We need model-infer call-level logs with hashed input pointers (not raw PII), and a separate immutable audit trail for administrative actions (who triggered failover / who exported snapshots). Security will send a sample log schema to Monica.

Cc'ing security so they can attach the schema and any other compliance docs.

Thanks,
Aisha Liao
Director, Platform Engineering | Nimbus Health
aisha.liao@nimbushealth.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Aisha Liao <aisha.liao@nimbushealth.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Nimbus Health Security <security@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-30T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: RE: APAC-first pin vs global-fallback scenarios — technical clarifications

Aisha / Sergio — thanks for the quick clarifications. Security schema from Nimbus would be helpful. A few technical notes and requests from our infra side so we can create an accurate ops proposal: 

1) Region pin behavior (short version):
- Pinning at the "model endpoint" level ensures traffic and persistent model state (KV caches, checkpoints) are kept within the pinned region.
- We support per-customer and per-route pinning. For your use case we typically pin patient-facing endpoints to APAC.

2) Failover modes and impact: 
- Manual cold failover (recommended for your runbook): RTO = 6–12 hours (restore from encrypted snapshots to a standby pool in fallback region then bring endpoints up); RPO = 24 hours if using daily incremental + weekly full.
- Automated warm-failover (not allowed per your policy): RTO = 15–45 minutes, RPO = <1 hour. Requires synchronous replication and warm standby capacity (materially higher cost).

3) Backups & key management:
- We can support snapshots encrypted with CMK (customer KMS/HSM) per account; Redwood never holds plaintext keys.
- Cross-region snapshot transfer is configurable: (a) disabled (APAC-only), (b) APAC-secondary-only, (c) global (US/EU) with documented triggers. You selected option (b) with a preference for APAC-secondary.

4) Logging and PII handling:
- Model-infer logs can be stored as hashes/pointers by default; raw inputs can be persisted in a separate, encrypted bucket only if requested. We recommend hashed pointers plus a short-lived debug retention when needed.

Action items for Nimbus to help us finalize: 
- Provide the explicit list of endpoints that must be APAC-pinned (endpoint names or route ids).
- Confirm backup transfer option: APAC-secondary-only (b) or APAC-only (a).
- Share any required RTO SLA thresholds that would force us to propose a warm-standby design.

I've attached a short explainer that maps the modes to expected cost deltas (redwood-region-pin-explainer.pdf). I will draft a simple "residency heatmap" once we have endpoint list + backup option.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwoodinference.com

I've uploaded the initial matrix and heatmap starter for your review: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB4xQ-residency-matrix. Please add comments directly on the sheet; Monica will iterate.

Sergio
